RewardsCompetitionsNewslettersWeather ForecastEuropeUkraine destroys section of Putin’s Crimea bridge in fierce exchangePart of key Russian road crossing collapses and parallel rail bridge damaged while Moscow hits infrastructure in Ukrainian capitalImages appear to show the road section of the Kerch bridge linking Crimea and Russia has collapsed following attacks by Ukraine. Photograph: Ukrainska Pravda/X Christopher Miller in KyivKatya Arenina in VilniusTue Nov 17 2026 - 18:19 • 4 MIN READUkrainian forces destroyed a key section of a bridge prized by president Vladimir Putin that links Crimea with southwest Russia as the two sides exchanged fierce strikes overnight on critical infrastructure.

Ukraine’s drones and missiles collapsed a crucial span of the road bridge across the Kerch Strait while damaging the rail bridge that runs in parallel, according to Ukrainian officials and videos and photos circulating on social media. It was the second Ukrainian strike on the bridge in two days.

Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskiy on Tuesday morning thanked his military and arms manufacturers for the “unprecedented operation”. He shared a video of a Flamingo FP-5 cruise missile flying towards the arch of the bridge that was destroyed, along with footage of an explosion.

Crucially, he said, the missile was flown with a “communications uplink” that “worked flawlessly until the very last seconds,” suggesting that Kyiv had found a potential alternative to Elon Musk’s Starshield satellite system that has been restricted for more than a week.

Since Moscow’s full-scale invasion in 2022, the bridge has served as a crucial military supply route for Russian forces in southern Ukraine.

Grateful to the Security Service of Ukraine, all units of Ukraine’s Defense Forces involved, Ukraine’s Minister of Defense, the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine and the General Staff, and all our weapons manufacturers for an unprecedented operation in response to… pic.twitter.com/pgUxGrE61K

Ukraine had spent several weeks disabling the Russian radars, air defence and electronic warfare systems that protect the bridge in a seven-stage operation, Zelenskiy said.

Sergei Aksyonov, the Moscow-installed governor of occupied Crimea, published a statement overnight about limits to traffic over the bridge because of the attack, adding in the morning that two people had been killed in the area.

Videos circulating online showed a Ukrainian drone striking the bridge, causing a large explosion. Photos showed the arch and the four-lane roadway that it had held up collapsed into the Kerch Strait.

The arch fell into the Kerch-Yenikale Canal, which forms the main deepwater shipping passage between the Sea of Azov and Black Sea, according to maritime security company Ambrey. Merchant ships were unable to use the channel, Ambrey said, further disrupting grain, fuel and fertiliser shipments from Russia, which have already been significantly curtailed owing to strikes.

Salvage operations would be challenging but the Russians could try to lift the arch from the water, said Tomas Alexa, maritime security analyst at Ambrey.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Tuesday that the bridge would be restored and would be “even better than before”.

The Crimean Bridge, also known as the Kerch Bridge, was Putin’s signature infrastructure project, intended to celebrate Russia’s 2014 annexation of Crimea. He opened the bridge by driving a truck across its 19km length in 2018.

For Ukraine, it is a symbol of Russia’s occupation. Kyiv first attacked it in October 2022, when a bomb in a truck exploded, severely damaging part of the structure and killing five people.

Moscow has used the bridge to transform Crimea into a crucial military base from which it launched its ground invasion almost five years ago, as well as drone and missile attacks on the country in the years since. Supplies have been brought into the occupied peninsula via truck and rail over the bridge.

Russia’s government press service said on Tuesday that deputy prime minister Marat Khusnullin would shortly meet a government commission dealing with the aftermath of the attack. The country’s Investigative Committee opened a criminal case over what it called an act of terrorism.

Russia’s defence ministry reported that 1,441 drones had been intercepted overnight, making it the largest Ukrainian drone attack of the war. The previous record was set a day earlier.

Meanwhile, four Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv’s Southern Bridge and three struck the Northern Bridge shortly before midnight on Monday, according to Zelenskiy.

A senior Ukrainian official said that preliminary intelligence reports suggested the missiles were provided to Russia by North Korea.

Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said experts were “determining the extent of damage”. The overnight attack overnight also “caused damage to critical infrastructure systems”, disrupting water and heating supplies, he said.

Russia has intensified its strikes on bridges over the Dnipro river in recent weeks, in what Zelenskiy said was an attempt to cut the country in half and make life unbearable for Ukrainians.

The Russian bombardment came a week after US-brokered peace talks between Washington, Kyiv and Moscow ended without a breakthrough – and hours after US president Donald Trump told reporters that Putin “could be tougher” on Ukraine.

“I think he’s backing down a little bit,” Trump said. “I think he could be a lot tougher, frankly.”

Trump is set to meet Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping together on the sidelines of a gathering of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in China’s southern city of Shenzhen on Thursday.

Trump said on Monday that the three leaders would discuss nuclear arms control, Iran and his “favourite subject”, Ukraine.

Yuri Ushakov, the Russian president’s foreign policy adviser, said on Monday that the Kremlin and White House were arranging a separate meeting between Putin and Trump, during which they would also discuss the war in Ukraine.

On Monday, Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, who is leading negotiations between Moscow and Kyiv, said he had spoken by phone with Ushakov, as well as Ukrainian and European partners, “to discuss the progress we have made and the next steps in the peace process”.

Kushner and Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff are expected in Berlin on Thursday to meet Ukrainian officials and the new eight-member European negotiating team to brief them on the talks in Shenzhen, US and Ukrainian officials said.

A US official said the Berlin meetings “will focus on further developing credible postwar security guarantees for Ukraine, advancing a comprehensive economic recovery and prosperity plan, and preparing for the next round of multilateral negotiations”. – Copyright The Financial Times Limited 2026
